note: Monthly reviews of the paper stock portfolio and paper/real options. Research, not advice. All figures from repo data (portfolio.json 10/30 close, paper-options-log.csv, degen-log.csv, live-account/ledger.csv). Written for Pedro: plain English, ideas split into needs_ok (rule changes he must approve) and auto (things done within the current rules), plus one 'strategy' line. Format: see README 'Monthly review format'.

reviews.title: October 2026
reviews.headline: Stocks ended October at $17,119.24 on $17,400 put in (down 1.61%), but $110.09 ahead of putting the same deposits into SPY ($17,009.15). Paper options traded by the rules made +$3,801; the one-off same-day trade outside the rules lost $2,968.

stats.label: Ahead of the same deposits in SPY

items: The plan is 60% Safe Core, 20% Diversifier and 20% Aggressive. At the Oct 30 close, the money invested was 47.2% Safe Core, 16.7% Diversifier and 36.2% Aggressive. Another $1,400 (8.2% of the total) was cash.
So Aggressive is about 16 points too high and Safe Core about 13 points too low. The reason: 8 of our 12 dip buys ($4,000 of $6,000) went into Aggressive stocks.
The biggest single holdings are SMH (7.64% of the total) and NVDA (6.12%). Both are under the 10% limit per holding.
We made 12 dip buys of $500 each. At the Oct 30 close they were worth $109.69 less than we paid. 3 were up (VRT +18.63%, ITA +2.01%, the Oct 30 VXUS buy +0.47%) and 9 were down.

Buys after a pullback from the recent high (7 buys) were up $32.16 combined. Buys at a price floor, called support (5 buys), all lost, −$141.85 combined, because the floors kept breaking after we bought.
We bought too much of two stocks: GEV twice (Oct 16 and Oct 20) and NVDA twice (Oct 20 and Oct 21). All four of those buys are down 6–8%.
Missed: VOO never got a dip buy, so Safe Core fell further behind. Some stocks qualified but the cash ran out first; TSM, AVGO and GEV are lined up for Friday, Nov 6.

14 trades by the rules, 7 winners, +$3,801. The $5,000 practice budget is now $8,801. 3 more planned trades were cancelled before buying: NVDA on Oct 27 never hit its entry signal, and TSLA on Oct 26 and AMD on Oct 28 were too big for the size check.

Worked best: trades planned ahead and bought at the open, +$2,128 across 6 (AMD put +$1,217, META call +$702, NVDA call +$660). The COIN earnings bet (a call and a put together) made +$902, but that's only one try.
Worked worst: puts bought after a stock that opened lower failed to climb back above its opening price. 4 trades, 1 winner (SPCX +$846), 3 losers, −$9 overall.

The one-time same-day QQQ call on Oct 16 (outside the rules) lost $2,968. It was bought after the broker's cutoff, so it wasn't a realistic fill. The real Robinhood account only did a $1 test buy-and-sell plus $0.09 in fees; it was worth $500.91 on Oct 30.

Mistakes that repeated: early trades broke the rules (a made-up stop, a buy at the open without its signal, picks made after the open, closing early on a feeling). Most later slips were in record-keeping and were caught before reporting.

needs_ok.do: Put some Friday cash into Safe Core (VOO, BND, SCHD) even without a dip, until Aggressive drifts back toward 20%.
needs_ok.why: Aggressive is about 16 points over the plan. This changes the buy rules.

needs_ok.do: Stop making support (price-floor) buys on their own. Wait for the pullback rule plus a day that closes back above the floor.
Allow at most two dip buys per stock per month.
needs_ok.why: The doubled-up GEV and NVDA buys are all down 6–8%.

needs_ok.do: Pause the failed-open puts until we've reviewed those 4 trades.
needs_ok.why: 3 of 4 lost (−$9 overall). Pausing a setup changes the options rulebook.

auto.do: Keep taking the planned trades at the open as they are.
auto.why: They were the best performer: +$2,128 across 6 trades.

auto.do: Keep earnings bets (a call and a put together) at the low-confidence size the rules already allow.
auto.why: Only one try so far (COIN, +$902), so it's too early to bet bigger.

auto.do: Write up a review of the 4 failed-open put trades for you.
auto.why: So you can decide on the pause above with the details in front of you.

auto.do: Buy TSM, AVGO and GEV on Friday, Nov 6 only if they still meet the pullback rule that day.
auto.why: They qualified in October, but the cash ran out first.

reviews.strategy: What this means for the strategy: the signals that held up were pullback buys and the planned trades at the open; support buys and failed-open puts were the weak signals. November tests whether tightening those two (with your OK) and steering cash back to Safe Core improves results, and next month's review will compare.
